tldr: For the complete causal current-status class, certified total observable procedures and a normalized full-experiment converse give matching absolute minimax risk and honest connected-interval length at \(\ell_n=\max\{n^{-1/3},n^{-2(\alpha+\beta)/(d+2\alpha+3\beta)}\}\) on explicit regions. The global-count route proves cube-root order for \(\alpha+\beta>d/3\), including \(d=\alpha=1\). For \(d>\alpha\), the two-time-scale pair route matches whenever \(\gamma\ge\min\{1/3,\rho\}\). Its cube-root sufficient conditions are \(4\alpha+3\beta\ge d\) and \(18\alpha\beta+4\alpha d\ge d^2\); in the rough region its exact proved matching condition is \(4\alpha^2+12\alpha\beta+6\alpha d-3\beta d-d^2\ge0\). The first cube-root condition is necessary, but is not proved to be the exact elbow. Residual rates, necessary logarithms, and all-procedure benefits of global assignments remain open.
gap: Adjusted current-status survival theory controls nuisance remainders under rate and derivative conditions; localized higher-order theory controls a different inspection and design-weight geometry. Neither opened theorem determines the full fixed-class causal marginal-median risk and honest-length frontier.
